title: A lockfile over what the run trusts, checked on every run
description: Every run hashes the files that decide what green means - the task contracts, the tests mapped to them or matched by the gate command, and the harness config - and compares them with .general-harness/lock.json. A test edited to get green, a config gate swapped for `true`, or a contract quietly changed shows up as a named failure instead of a green run.

clauses.text: --lock writes .general-harness/lock.json holding a lock schema version and a sha256 for every task contract, every test file mapped to a unit or matched by the gate test command, and the harness config.
clauses.observable_by: writeLock on a temp project produces a lock whose files map lists exactly those paths with 64-hex hashes and whose version is LOCK_VERSION

clauses.text: Every run recomputes the hashes, and a changed, added or removed locked file is a FAIL leg that names the file.
clauses.observable_by: runMatrix after editing a locked test returns a FAIL lock leg whose breaker names that path; adding and removing a file are named the same way

clauses.text: A missing lock is allowed only when the strictest tier across the selected contracts is quick; otherwise the run is BLOCKED with a message to run --lock.
clauses.observable_by: runMatrix with no lock gives a SKIP lock leg for quick-only contracts and a BLOCKED leg mentioning --lock when any selected contract is standard

clauses.text: --relock --reason rewrites the lock, appends {time, reason, changed} to lock-history.jsonl and reports what changed; --relock without a reason is refused, and --lock over an existing drifted lock refuses and points to --relock.
clauses.observable_by: relock appends one history line carrying the reason and the changed paths; writeLock over drift and relock with no reason both throw, naming --relock and --reason

clauses.text: A gate command that is trivially true - true, exit 0, :, an echo, or empty - is a FAIL with a reason saying it tests nothing.
clauses.observable_by: isTrivialCommand accepts each of those forms and rejects a real runner; runMatrix with config gate.test "true" returns a FAIL test leg with that reason

clauses.text: A file checked out with CRLF line endings hashes the same as its LF form, so a Windows checkout does not read as drift.
clauses.observable_by: hashFile gives the same digest for the CRLF and LF forms of one text

clauses.text: The command line exposes --lock, --relock and --reason, and prints what changed.
clauses.observable_by: spawning general-verify --lock writes the lock, --lock after an edit exits 1 naming --relock, and --relock --reason exits 0 naming the changed file

non_goals: Protecting source files under test. The builder is meant to change those; the lock covers what decides whether the change is accepted.
Stopping a human from relocking. --relock is the legal path and leaves a reasoned trail in lock-history.jsonl.
